title: Fake Amazon Phone Call Scam
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Amazon, saying there is a problem with your account or a suspicious charge. They try to get your personal or bank information or ask you to download software on your computer.
example_message: "This is Amazon Security. We noticed a suspicious charge on your account. Please press 1 to speak to a representative."
red_flags: Requests for personal or payment information
what_to_do: Hang up and call Amazon directly using the number on their website.

title: Medicare Card Renewal Text Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying your Medicare card needs to be renewed or updated. The message includes a link that leads to a fake website asking for your Medicare number and other personal details.
example_message: "Your Medicare card is expiring soon. Click here to update your information: [fake link]"
what_to_do: Do not click the link or reply; contact Medicare using the number on your card if you have questions.

title: Facebook Grandchild Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Scammers hack or create fake Facebook accounts pretending to be your grandchild. They message you saying they are in trouble and need money right away, often for bail or a medical emergency.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in trouble and need money for bail. Please don’t tell mom and dad. Can you send $1,000 right away?"
red_flags: Asked to keep it a secret
Unusual payment methods like gift cards or wire transfer
what_to_do: Call your grandchild or another family member directly to check before sending any money.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Up
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and must call a number for help. The scammer tries to get you to pay for fake repairs or gives them access to your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Phone number to call for help
Asked to give remote access to your computer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; use your own trusted tech support if you need help.

title: IRS Tax Refund Email Phishing
how_it_works: You receive an email claiming to be from the IRS about a tax refund. The email asks you to click a link and enter personal information, but it is a trick to steal your identity.
example_message: "You are eligible for a tax refund. Click here to claim your refund now."
red_flags: Email claims to be from the IRS
Requests for personal or bank information
what_to_do: Do not click any links or give information; the IRS will never email you about refunds.
